### 2. README Content (Setup Instructions)

The README is a comprehensive contest instruction document (not yet customized for the team). Key setup steps:

- **Repo init command:** `repo init -u https://github.com/open-vela/contest2026_434_TinyMind -b dev-ai-contest-2026 -m contest2026_434_TinyMind.xml` followed by `repo sync -c -j8`
- **Build command:** `./build.sh <board-config-path> [menuconfig|distclean] [-j8]` from the openvela workspace root (parent directory of the contest repo)
- **Submission deadline:** September 20, 2026
- **Submission method:** Fork the repo, develop, commit, push, then open a PR back to the main branch (can self-merge)

The manifest file (`contest2026_434_TinyMind.xml`) defines symlinks:
- `app/hello_app` maps to `packages/demos/contest2026_434_hello_app`
- `quickapp/hello_quickapp` maps to `packages/apps/contest2026_434_hello_quickapp`
- `board/contest_board` maps to `vendor/openvela/boards/contest2026_434_board`

---

### 3. Board/Vendor Code (SF32LB52)

There is a `board/contest_board/` directory containing a **generic contest board skeleton**, but **no SF32LB52-specific code exists**. The board skeleton includes:
- `board/contest_board/src/board_boot.c` -- a minimal boot file (337 bytes)
- `board/contest_board/configs/nsh/defconfig` -- a minimal NSH defconfig (152 bytes)
- `board/contest_board/Kconfig` and `CMakeLists.txt` -- build integration files

This is a template board placeholder. There is no SF32LB52 vendor code, no chip-specific drivers, and no BSP for any specific hardware in this repository. The actual vendor/chip code would come from the full openvela source tree pulled via `repo sync`.

---

### 4. logs/ Directory

Yes, the `logs/` directory exists with a **placeholder structure** (no real AI coding logs yet):
- `logs/README.md` -- describes the log submission format
- `logs/your-github-login/` -- placeholder directory (teams must rename to their actual GitHub username)
- `logs/your-github-login/manifest.json` -- a manifest template
- `logs/your-github-login/2026-01-01/claude-code__example.jsonl` -- an example log file

The log format requires: `<github_login>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<tool>__<session-id>.jsonl` where tool names are `claude-code`, `opencode`, `codex`, or `kiro`.

### 5. .claude/ Directory

**No `.claude/` directory exists** in the repository. There are no skills, settings, or Claude-specific configuration files.

### 6. CLA / Contributor Agreement

There is **no standalone CLA file** in the repo, but there is a **CLA GitHub Actions workflow** at `.github/workflows/cla.yml`. It:
- Triggers on `pull_request_target` (opened, reopened, synchronize) and issue comments containing `/check-cla`
- Delegates to a shared reusable workflow at `open-vela/public-actions/.github/workflows/cla.yml@dev`
- The README states: "First-time contributors must sign the CLA at https://openvela.com/#/community/cla; PRs automatically run `cla/signature` checks; after signing, comment `/check-cla` in the PR to re-verify."
